An approaching Atlantic frontal system is bringing persistent cloud cover, widespread rain (locally 5–17 mm), and southwesterly winds of 10–25 mph (gusts higher), which limit daytime solar heating and promote mixing that prevents temperatures from exceeding the mid-teens to low 20s °C. This follows warmer conditions on September 4 (daytime highs 20–22 °C) as the system arrives overnight. 

Climatologically, the September 5 average high is 18.5 °C, and current model consensus places tomorrow near or slightly below that baseline due to the overcast, rainy regime. Traders appear to have incorporated the latest model updates showing limited variability in peak temperatures, favoring the narrow 17–19 °C band while assigning low odds to outliers above 20 °C or below 16 °C. Updated forecast guidance or radar trends on the morning of September 5 could still shift the final observed high within the leading range.

Afternoon temperatures hinge on the timing and extent of increasing high cloud cover, which several ensembles show arriving by midday and limiting peak insolation, alongside dew-point values near 8–11°C that keep the boundary layer relatively dry. Minor spread in guidance—some runs reaching 29–30°C while others cap near 27–28°C—reflects uncertainty in exact cloud thickness and southeasterly advection strength. Updated short-range model cycles and official Météo-France briefings expected in the next 24–48 hours will likely tighten the range ahead of resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, widespread rain, and northerly winds are suppressing daytime heating across the Tokyo region ahead of September 6, keeping official forecast highs clustered between 23–25 °C according to multiple numerical models. The dominant low-pressure system and associated frontal activity limit solar insolation and enhance evaporative cooling, preventing the higher temperatures typical for early September. Market-implied odds favor 24 °C (34 %) and 25 °C (30.5 %) because small differences in the timing and intensity of heaviest rainfall or wind gusts can shift the daily maximum by 1 °C. Traders weigh the consensus of global and regional models against the narrow uncertainty range created by variable cloud breaks or slight steering-pattern shifts before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from the Hong Kong Observatory and ensemble model guidance indicate a maximum temperature of 30–31°C on September 6, driven by a weakening continental airstream over southern China that favors partly cloudy skies with limited afternoon heating. Scattered showers expected during the day, with medium rain probability, introduce uncertainty by increasing cloud cover and evaporative cooling that can suppress peak readings. Historical September climatology shows typical highs near 30°C, and current model consensus aligns closely with this baseline while noting minor steering influences from distant tropical systems like Krovanh. Updated runs in the next 24–48 hours will clarify whether reduced insolation holds the high at 30°C or permits brief clearing to reach 31°C.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the San Francisco International Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=ksfo

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and local model guidance indicate a persistent marine layer and moderate onshore westerly flow will limit daytime heating in San Francisco on September 6, keeping the high temperature most likely in the upper 60s. This pattern aligns with climatological norms for early September, when average highs near 70°F can be suppressed by coastal stratus and sea-breeze effects. Current forecasts from multiple sources cluster between 67–68°F, supporting the market’s heaviest volume on the 68–69°F bin. A modest warming trend is expected after Labor Day as the marine layer weakens, but no significant offshore flow or ridge strengthening is projected before the 6th. Updated model runs and NWS briefings over the next 48 hours will refine the exact peak and determine whether readings edge into the low 70s.

A strong cold air advection event, driven by persistent southwesterly to southerly flow behind a frontal passage, has sharply lowered temperatures from the seasonal norm. Clear conditions overnight have allowed efficient radiational cooling, while modest insolation and the cool air mass constrain afternoon peaks. Historical September averages near 19–20°C provide context for how unusual this early-spring chill is.

Model consensus remains tight with low precipitation risk and no major forecast shifts anticipated before resolution, supporting the narrow probability distribution around 10–12°C. Minor upside risk to 12–13°C exists if winds weaken or cloud cover increases, but current data favor the lower end of that range.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=mpmg

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from agencies like the Instituto de Meteorología e Hidrología de Panamá points to a maximum temperature in Panama City on September 6 near 30–32°C, with ensemble spreads reflecting uncertainty from variable cloud cover and convective activity tied to lingering tropical moisture. High humidity levels near 80% and potential afternoon thunderstorms, typical for the September wet season under neutral ENSO conditions, can limit peak heating through reduced insolation, while clearer intervals allow stronger diurnal warming. Historical September averages hover around 30°C, and the tightly clustered market-implied odds capture this narrow range amid modest forecast differences in steering patterns and precipitation timing. Updated runs ahead of the date will refine these probabilities.
